scope.supports: For every finite index types m, n, k and every commutative ring (kernel-checked, Matrix.fromBlocks), on the declared PAIR model of a complex matrix A = (P, Q) with the hand-written product (PS - QT, PT + QS): R is additive, ring-linear, multiplicative on composable matrices, sends the identity to the identity and is injective; J^2 = -1; J_m R(A) = R(A) J_n for rectangular A; R(iA) = J_m R(A); R(A*) = R(A)^T so A is Hermitian iff R(A) is symmetric; Tr R(A) = 2 Tr P, i.e. twice the REAL part of the complex trace (the instance A = 1 + i has complex trace 1 + i and real trace 2); Theorem 2: a matrix indexed by (m + m) x (n + n) is R(A) for exactly one A iff J_m M = M J_n; conjugating J by an invertible P transports the commutant, and an explicit unimodular instance shows [[1,-1],[2,-1]] is a second integer square root of -I that does not commute with J (kernel instance). Native (exact tables, not kernel theorems): 9 product cases up to 3 x 3 (square and rectangular, incl. A = 0, A = I, A = iI, a Hermitian A) with R(AB), R(A*) and the INTERLEAVED coordinate order (re_1, im_1, re_2, ...) which in general gives a different matrix from the block one (the two can coincide, e.g. for A = 0 or A = I); each product record states whether the interleaved matrix commutes with the block J_n, and no universal statement is made; 13 real matrices tested for membership in the image (positive cases, diag(1,0,0,0), diag(-1,1,1,1), diag(1,-1) and diag(I,-I) which anticommute with J, an odd-dimensional matrix, rectangular cases, a symmetric non-image matrix); 9 small matrices (8 Hermitian, 1 non-Hermitian refused) on which complex positive semidefiniteness and positive semidefiniteness of the real symmetric R(A) agree (instances of preservation and reflection, found by principal minors and by elimination; NOT a kernel theorem); the J-structure flags of 8 integer 2 x 2 matrices; and a brute-force census of the integer square roots of -I in the boxes B = 1, 2, 3, 5, 7: 26 solutions in the box [-5,5], of which only +-J commute with J. The census is a bounded enumeration, not a theorem; "only +-J commute with J" is shown by the census in those boxes only (the commutant of J in M_2(Z) is {aI + bJ}, but that argument is not in the module).
scope.does_not_support: Any selection of J or of the complex field (J is a declaration; a second square root of -I exists in the kernel instance and the census exhibits many more); the identification of the pair model CMat with Mathlib complex matrices (no anchor shows CMat is an associative ring or equals Matrix m n Complex); the block-ordering convention (all real coordinates before all imaginary ones) is part of the definition: the interleaved ordering gives a different J and a different matrix; states sigma = R(rho)/2, positivity as a theorem (native instances only), effects, instruments / Kraus intertwining (Theorem 3), the balanced tensor lift, or any operational or physical reading; infinite dimensions; the claim that every real channel is a realified complex one (it is not).
scope.narrowest_claim: Complex matrices here are the declared pair model (P, Q) with the hand-written product. R(A) = [[P,-Q],[Q,P]] is an injective ring-linear multiplicative embedding of these into real matrices with J_m R(A) = R(A) J_n and Tr R(A) = 2 Re Tr A, and its image is exactly the real matrices that intertwine the DECLARED J (block coordinate order); the same J^2 = -1 identity holds for other matrices (kernel instance, bounded census), so the choice of J remains an input.
scope.next_test: Prove in the kernel that R preserves and reflects positivity for Hermitian A, i.e. A is positive semidefinite iff the real quadratic form of R(A) is nonnegative, and that sigma = R(rho)/2 has real trace 1 exactly when Tr rho = 1; the native psd rows are the instances to match.
